english:
Alleluia, Psalm 23 [24]: "Remember, O Lord, your compassion."
Gospel according to Matthew 9:1 to verse 8: "And getting into a boat..." to "...authority to men."

In the Evening
First Psalm 50 [51]: "Create in me a clean heart."
Antiphon: "Have mercy on me, O God."
Gospel according to John 20:19 to verse 23: "And it was evening..." to "...shall be retained."
Messedi: "Let your hand be..." [and] "You who shepherd."
Hambartsi [Hymn of Ascent], Tone 8 [d-k]: "I harasharzh" (Ի հարաշարժ).
Dismissal Psalm 142 [143]: "Let your good spirit..."
Antiphon: "Lord, hear."
Gospel according to John 3:1 to verse 8: "And there was a man..." to "...of the Spirit."

[Decorative Divider]

Saturday, Tone 8 [d-k]: "I harasharzh" (Ի հարաշարժ), with its canon.
Alleluia: "At your rebuke, O Lord" [and] "He sent from on high."
Antiphon: "Establish a clean heart in me" [and] "Cast me not away."
In the Morning, Psalm 22 [23]: "In green pastures."
Antiphon: "The Lord shall shepherd."
Proverbs 7:31 to verse 21: "Because of all..." to "...for clarity."
Prophet Isaiah 11:1 to verse 4: "And a rod shall come forth..." to "...the humble of the earth."
Catholic Epistle, 1 John 4:1 to verse 6: "Beloved, do not [believe] every..." to "...of deceit."
Alleluia, Psalm 142 [143]: "Let your good spirit."
Gospel according to Luke 4:14 to verse 22: "And Jesus returned..." to "...from his mouth."

Midday Liturgy
Introit: "We confess you, O God."
Hymn, Tone 8 [d-k]: "I harasharzh" (Ի հարաշարժ).
Psalm 39 [40]: "He drew me up."
Antiphon: "With patience."
Prophet Jeremiah 1:1 to verse 10: "The word of God..." to "...to build and to plant."
Again, Jeremiah 38:1 to verse 13: "And Shephatiah heard..." to "...in the court of the prison."
Catholic Epistle, 2 Peter 2:9 to verse 22: "The Lord knows..." to "...wallowing in the mire."
Alleluia, Psalm 67 [68]: "In the congregations."
Gospel according to Matthew 2:16 to verse 18: "Then when..." to "...because they were no more."

In the Evening
First Psalm 22 [23]: "The Lord shall shepherd."
Gospel according to John 3:1 to verse 6: "And there was a man..." to "...is spirit."
[Hymn] "Joyous Light" (Phos Hilaron).
Messedi: "God said..." [from] Exodus.
Hambartsi [Hymn of Ascent], Tone 5 [g-dz]: "The Holy Spirit was" (Հոգին սուրբ էր).
Dismissal Psalm 92 [93]: "The Lord reigns, he is robed in majesty."
Gospel according to John 3:32 to verse 34: "After this..." to "...God [gives] the Spirit."
Litany: "Let us ask" [and] "Save us."
Prayer: "King of peace."

[Decorative Divider]

From here until the third Sunday of Vardavar:
Everything set down remains always unchanged; only the Resurrection Hymns of the Fathers (Harts) change at times, which [you will find] in the Directory.

[Decorative Divider]

First Sunday of the Resurrection, Tone 1 [a-dz]: "Let us sing."
Resurrection Fathers Hymn (Harts), Tone 1 [a-dz]: "Who came for salvation."
Midday Introit: "Only-begotten Son."
Hymn, Tone 1 [a-dz]: "Christ, the King of glory."
Psalm 64 [65]: "Praise is due to you."
Scripture, 3 Kings [1 Kings] 18:29 to verse 46: "Elijah spoke..." to "...Jezreel."
Scripture, 4 Kings [2 Kings] 2:1 to verse 15: "And it came to pass when [the Lord] was about to take up..." to "...upon the earth."
Psalm 65 [66]: "All the earth."
Antiphon: "Shout with joy."
Catholic Epistle, James 5:16 to verse 20: "Confess..." to "...a multitude of sins."
Alleluia: "Arise, O Lord."
Gospel according to Luke 4:25 to verse 30: "But in truth..." to "...went through them."
In the Evening, Hambartsi [Hymn of Ascent], Tone 1 [a-dz]: "With the dawning."
And the rest is of the Resurrection.

Begin the Resurrection Hymns of Ascent (Hambartsis) from here: say them on Sundays according to the proper tone. And on whichever Sunday another feast should occur, when you do not take the Resurrection Hymn of Ascent, keep it in mind; when a Sunday occurs in that same tone, say both Hymns of Ascent, as the Directory shows you.

[Decorative Divider]

Monday, Tone 2 [a-k]. Of the Holy Hripsimean Virgins.

In the Evening, perform the Pre-festal Service (Nakhatonak): "Souls" (Անձինք), with its canon.
And during the night, Tone 6 [g-k]: "Dedicated souls" (Անձինք նուիրեալք).
Fathers Hymn (Harts), Tone 8 [d-k]: "Today the invincible," with its canon.
Morning Song: "Send out, Lord, your light."
Litany: "The great and powerful God."
Magnificat (Mankunk), Tone 6 [g-k]: "The remembrance of Christ."
Litany: "For peace."
Prayer: "Holy are you, Lord."
Antiphon: "I loved."
Song: "Of the Creator" (Ararchakan).
Supplication: "Christ our God."
Litany: "By the holy ascetics."
Prayer: "Crown-giver."
And then say "Arevelits" (Of the East) without fail. "Save us" (Ketso) is not used except on Sundays and Dominical Feasts.
Do likewise for all feasts of the martyrs.
